prompt:
Synthetic museum-administration exercise. An invented museum network has a conservation-review policy for loans. Explain which proposed loans require review and which facts remain unresolved. The curator has received a standard policy, a signed exception, an internal summary, and incomplete project records. This packet is a fictional closed rule system and is not advice about real contracts or cultural-property law.

[B20-S1: network policy effective March 1] A physical loan from a network museum to an outside institution requires conservation review if its insured value exceeds 50,000 units. Related physical loans for the same exhibition project, departing within any thirty-day interval, are aggregated before applying that threshold. “Related” means organized under the same exhibition agreement, not merely made by the same borrower. Digital image licenses are outside this physical-loan policy and are not added to insured loan value. Loans entirely between network museums are exempt from this review threshold. The policy does not abolish other approvals, and this packet supplies no rules for those other approvals.

[B20-S2: signed exception and delegation] An authorized network director signed an exception on April 10 for the named exhibition River Rooms. It permits that exhibition's physical loans to depart without threshold review until April 30 inclusive, provided every item is accompanied by an approved condition report. The exception does not waive the condition-report requirement and does not name any other exhibition. A delegation schedule allows local curators to certify condition reports but does not authorize them to extend director-signed exceptions. An email from a local curator says, “I am happy to keep this arrangement going into May.” No director approval of an extension appears in the packet.

[B20-S3: proposed transactions] Loan Ash, insured for 30,000, departs April 20 from a network museum to outside institution Harbor Hall under the River Rooms agreement; its condition report is approved. Loan Beech, insured for 25,000, departs April 28 to Harbor Hall under the same agreement, but its condition report is still awaiting certification. Loan Elm, insured for 35,000, departs May 5 to Harbor Hall. Its booking record uses project code RR-2, but the underlying exhibition agreement is missing; the packet does not establish whether RR-2 is part of River Rooms or a separate project. A digital-image license worth 20,000 is issued to Harbor Hall on April 21. Loan Fir, insured for 90,000, departs April 22 between two network museums.

[B20-S4: summaries and questions] An internal checklist says “all Harbor Hall loans are covered by the April exception” and tells staff to add image-license fees to insured values. Its author did not consult the signed exception. A planning note says Beech should be considered approved because certification is routine, but the certifier has not examined its condition report. A publicity sheet praises the exhibition's historical importance. Harbor Hall asks whether splitting a shipment over several dates avoids the threshold, while a registrar asks whether Elm's later departure invalidates the earlier loans retroactively.

Explain the threshold calculation and the exception's independent conditions. Distinguish borrower identity from exhibition identity, permission to certify from authority to extend, and a proposed or expected approval from an approval actually recorded. Give conditional conclusions for the missing Elm agreement without inventing it. Explain why an exception valid for qualifying departures in April is not automatically erased by a later May transaction, while the May transaction must be assessed under the applicable rule and aggregation window. Stay within conservation review rather than claiming every loan is fully authorized for all purposes.
response:
Ash qualifies for the April exception on the supplied facts. Beech cannot yet rely on it because its condition report is unapproved. Elm's May departure needs a separate assessment that depends on its missing exhibition agreement. None of these conclusions establishes approval for every purpose.

### Calculate by exhibition agreement and departure window

The ordinary rule requires conservation review when insured value **exceeds 50,000 units**. Related physical loans are added together when they depart within any thirty-day interval. “Related” means the same exhibition agreement; using the same borrower does not suffice. The window can cross a calendar-month boundary. [B20-S1]

Ash and Beech share the River Rooms agreement and depart eight days apart, so their relevant combined value is:

\[
30{,}000+25{,}000=55{,}000\text{ units}.
\]

That exceeds the threshold even though neither loan exceeds it individually. Splitting these shipments across April 20 and April 28 therefore does not avoid the ordinary review requirement. The 20,000-unit image license contributes nothing to this calculation because digital licenses are outside this policy. Fir's 90,000-unit transfer is exempt because it is entirely between network museums. [B20-S1; B20-S3]

### Apply the exception's conditions separately

The director's exception covers the named exhibition River Rooms, permits qualifying departures through **April 30 inclusive**, and requires an approved condition report for every item. Satisfying the exhibition and date conditions does not satisfy the report condition. The exception waives threshold review; it does not turn an unexamined report into an approved one. [B20-S2]

| Transaction | Conservation-review conclusion on the supplied record |
| --- | --- |
| **Ash — April 20** | Its River Rooms agreement, April departure, and approved condition report satisfy the stated exception. It may depart without threshold review under that exception. |
| **Beech — April 28** | Its report is still awaiting certification. If the required approval is actually obtained by departure, it can qualify for the April exception. Without that approval, it cannot rely on the exception, and the ordinary 55,000-unit aggregate triggers review. |
| **Elm — May 5** | The April exception does not cover its departure. Whether ordinary threshold review is required depends on the missing agreement, as explained below. |
| **Digital-image license — April 21** | Outside this physical-loan policy; excluded from the insured-value aggregate. |
| **Fir — April 22** | Exempt from this review threshold as a transfer between network museums. |

These conclusions use the transaction facts in [B20-S3] and the rules in [B20-S1; B20-S2]. Beech's expected routine certification is not a recorded approval. Local curators may certify condition reports, but their delegation does not allow them to extend a director-signed exception. The curator's email therefore supplies no authorized May extension. [B20-S2; B20-S4]

### Elm has two live possibilities

**If RR-2 belongs to the River Rooms agreement**, Elm, Ash, and Beech are related. April 20 through May 5 fits within a thirty-day interval, giving:

\[
30{,}000+25{,}000+35{,}000=90{,}000\text{ units}.
\]

Elm then requires threshold review: the aggregate exceeds 50,000 units, and its May 5 departure is outside the exception. The exception does not say to remove qualifying April loans from the aggregation calculation. [B20-S1–S3]

**If RR-2 is a separate exhibition agreement**, Elm is not aggregated with River Rooms merely because Harbor Hall is the borrower. Its supplied value is 35,000 units, below the threshold. On the listed transactions, threshold review would not be required; any additional related loans within the applicable window would still need checking. The booking code alone cannot settle which branch applies. [B20-S1; B20-S3]

Elm's later departure does not retroactively erase the exception for April departures that met its conditions. Aggregating earlier loans when assessing Elm is compatible with honoring their valid April waiver. If Beech never obtains its required report, its problem is its own unmet condition, not Elm's arrival in May. [B20-S1; B20-S2]

The internal checklist incorrectly substitutes borrower identity for exhibition identity and incorrectly includes image-license fees. The exhibition's historical importance changes none of the supplied conditions. Obtain Elm's underlying agreement and Beech's actual certification record to resolve the remaining questions. Other approvals may still apply, but their rules are absent from this packet. [B20-S1; B20-S3; B20-S4]
